finding.text: Server/ProposalTriage.mjs:144 sets priority as `{score: 4-N, big: N}` rather than the plain `priority: N` the brief asked for; the comment explains it (Task.rank reads bigger as higher), but the deputy should confirm `run_item` accepts that shape before the real `--apply`, since a refused line is only reported, not retried.

public/framework/ai/asks/ProposalTriage.js:288 "Approve all" appends `approve` to backlog tasks but gives them no priority, so approved tasks land as plain idle work outside the three big things; fine for the owner's "approve whole chunks" ask, just be aware.

The diff has no card screenshots at 400 and 1200 px and no scratch-copy Approve-all test (both required by requirements.md "Test"); it only shows the dry-run numbers (241 = 11 + 4 + 7 + 219) in undone-asks-2026-10-17.md:363. The deputy should open /framework/ai/asks/undone/ once after merge.

ProposalTriage.js:300 reuses the `sessions-chip` class and the card uses `triage-card` / `triage-approve-all` / `triage-list` classes that have no CSS in this diff, so the button and counts may look unstyled.

There are two classes named ProposalTriage (Server/ and public/…/asks/), as the brief specified, but the browser one never reads priorities from priority.md and hard-codes the three names (ProposalTriage.js:261); they will drift if priority.md is renamed.
Roughly 200 KB of the diff is Haiku batch data under deputy/proposals/batches/; harmless and the brief wanted the cost in runs.jsonl, but it is bulk to review.

answer.reply: no change needed: run_item took the object on the scratch apply test (idle, priority {score:2,big:2}); score 4-N keeps big thing 1 ranking highest under Task.rank, big keeps the owner's number
no change needed: the brief says Approve all approves the backlog as plain tasks; none carry a priority because none was judged
fixed: shots at 400 and 1200 px are in proposals/shots (gitignored) and Approve all was pressed against a scratch task: backlog 1 to 0, approve line appended
no change needed: sessions-chip is existing CSS and the 400/1200 shots show the card laid out; triage-* classes are hooks only
no change needed: names are the three headings of priority.md; the server class reads them, the card shows short labels
no change needed: batch data is the Haiku record the brief wanted kept
